name: Poojaa Precision Engg. Ltd
title: Poojaa Precision Engg. Ltd - 544844 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Maiden call from a small aluminium precision caster: H1 FY27 revenue INR210 crore (+68%) and EBITDA margin 19%, with 82% utilisation and a new plant that doubles capacity, but guidance is aspirational and unaudited by numbers.

summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue rose 68% YoY to INR210 crores and PAT 88% to INR25 crores, with an INR1,180 crore order book backing a 50% FY27 growth target.
summary.overview: Poojaa Precision Engineering reported its maiden earnings call for H1 FY27 (half year ended September 30, 2026). Revenue from operations reached INR210 crores versus INR125 crores in H1 FY26, with EBITDA of INR40 crores (19% margin) and PAT of INR25 crores (12% margin). Non-automotive revenue grew 194% YoY to INR53 crores, lifting its share to 25% of sales from 15%. Management reiterated a target of about 50% growth in FY27, 30-35% CAGR thereafter, and INR1,000 crores of turnover by FY30, while capacity is being nearly doubled by FY28.

financial_highlights.change: +68% YoY vs INR125 crores in H1 FY26
FY24 INR174 crores; FY25 INR222 crores; 30% CAGR
Last month sales INR42 crores; die stock INR20 crores

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Serves two-wheeler, three-wheeler, passenger and commercial vehicle components (intake manifolds, cylinder heads, crankcases, transmission housings) and EV parts. Accounted for 63% of H1 FY27 sales and about 52% of the INR1,180 crore order book; management said margin contribution was about 40% of H1 profit.

segments.name: Non-automotive / Engineering
segments.commentary: Covers power and energy distribution, agriculture, defence, healthcare and heavy engineering. Revenue of INR53 crores in H1 FY27 (25% of sales) and about 48% of the order book; contributed about 60% of H1 margins per management. Energy is the largest non-auto sector, followed by agriculture and healthcare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 50% over FY26 (INR294 crores base), as reiterated on the call.
Revenue CAGR of 30-35% for FY28-FY30, with a target of INR1,000 crores annual turnover by FY30.
Order book execution path: about INR630-640 crores next year, INR800-820 crores the year after, and about INR1,000 crores by 2030 (management's framing).
Long-term mix target of 50:50 auto to non-auto within 2-3 years, and a longer-term 33:33:33 split across auto, EV and engineering.

Management expects all fixed costs of Unit 3 to be absorbed, so future margins should be driven by variable costs; it also said debt would be fully repaid by Q2 FY28, with finance cost minimal thereafter.
Aerospace (HAL / Indian Air Force) business expected to reach production in at least four years; defence to be served from Unit 3.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR1,180 crore order book split across H2 FY27, FY28 and FY29, and what does it include?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the book is about 52% auto and 48% non-auto, with execution of INR630-640 crore next year, INR800-820 crore the year after, and about INR1,000 crore by 2030, implying 30-35% CAGR.

qa_highlights.question: How much casting capacity will be installed this year and next, and what utilisation is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Machines are booked and expected by September 2027, with about 20% of the new capacity used this year and full installation next year; utilisation to ramp through 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Is aerospace business serviced from current or new capacity, and what is its timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: HAL approved the company for prototype parts and the Indian Air Force cleared its audit; production expected in at least four years, with aerospace moving to a separate Unit 4 and defence served from Unit 3.

qa_highlights.question: How is aluminium price movement handled in COGS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts with customers pass through metal price changes, so there is no net impact on performance; a later analyst question also got confirmation of full pass-through with a time lag.

qa_highlights.question: Will working capital normalise, and is the inventory build a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about INR60 crore versus last month's sales of INR42 crore (about 45 days), including INR20 crore of die stock with a 6-9 month cycle; management said dies will remain at 7-8% of sales and the normal cycle should stay near one month.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin split between auto and non-auto, and how will it evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: In H1 FY27 non-auto contributed about 60% of margins and auto about 40%; management declined to quantify margin by sub-sector, citing product-mix changes over the next 6-8 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the basis for the INR1,000 crore FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a RFQ pipeline above INR2,000 crore a year, an 8-10% strike rate, INR160-180 crore of new business added annually, and five demand drivers (China+1, Make in India, lightweighting, EV, aluminium substitution).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth target and PAT margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated about 50% growth in FY27, 30-35% CAGR in FY28-30; debt to be fully repaid by Q2 FY28, with PAT margins expected to rise as fixed costs are absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offloading charge in other expenses (around 10% of revenue)?
qa_highlights.answer: Simple components are machined outside, while critical machining and processes such as powder coating, surface treatment and tooling are offloaded to optimise in-house capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mix of GDC, LPDC and HPDC, and the alloy sourcing split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 70% GDC and 25% LPDC with 5% HPDC (later corrected); about 40% of alloy is bought as primary and converted, and 60% is bought as ready alloys from validated customer-linked sources.

capex_capacity: Current installed capacity about 13,800 MT melting and 6,000 MT casting and finishing; expected to rise to 28,800 MT and 12,600 MT by FY28, nearly doubling capacity.

Monthly capacity cited as 500 tons existing plus 110 tons from new capacity (20%), total 610 tons per month for casting and machining; September 2026 output about 480 tons, current month expected above 500 tons; utilisation about 82% including expanded capacity.

Pre-new-plant utilisation about 80-82%, which management said drove the Unit 3 investment; H1 casting utilisation cited by an analyst at 71-72% versus about 84% last year (not disputed by management).
Machines booked post-IPO; management expects delivery by September 2027 with about 20% of new capacity utilised in the current year and full installation next year, ramping to 2030 targets.
Management said no additional capacity beyond Unit 3 is needed for INR1,000 crore turnover by 2030; aerospace work to be served from a separate Unit 4 after about four years.
Management said all fixed costs of Unit 3 are already absorbed, so future cost increases will be variable-cost driven; debt to be repaid by Q2 FY28.
demand_pricing: Order book of about INR1,180 crore: about 52% auto and 48% non-auto/engineering; management guided execution of about INR630-640 crore next year, INR800-820 crore the year after, and about INR1,000 crore by 2030.
Management said it files RFQs worth more than INR2,000 crore a year at an 8-10% strike rate, adding INR160-180 crore of new business annually over the last three years.
Revenue mix H1 FY27: auto 62-63% and non-auto 37-38%; H1 FY26 auto 72% and non-auto 28%. Target 50:50 in 2-3 years and 33:33:33 auto/EV/engineering in the long term.
Non-auto margins: management said non-auto contributed about 60% of H1 FY27 margins and auto about 40%.
Energy (power distribution) is the largest non-auto sector, grew from about INR17 crore to INR48 crore in H1; agriculture second, healthcare third; defence expected to add over the next 2 years.

Aluminium: management said customer contracts pass through raw material cost movements fully, so no P&L impact; gross margin fell from 59% to 53% due to product mix shifting to bigger parts (50-80 kg vs 1-9 kg earlier).
Customer base expanded from 39 in FY24 to 58 in H1 FY27; about 7-8% of sales come from die sales; H1 has historically been 43-47% of full-year revenue.
risks_watch: Tender-based nature of power and energy business; management says Fortune 500 panel status smooths demand but no order split by sub-sector was given.
Gross margin compression (59% to 53%) with product mix shifting to heavier castings; management said margin direction will be clearer in 6-8 months.
Execution risk on Unit 3 machine delivery (targeted September 2027) and ramp-up to 28,800 MT melting capacity by FY28.
Aerospace (HAL / IAF) qualification timeline of at least four years, with R&D on magnesium alloys still at prototype stage and no revenue modelled.
Aluminium price pass-through and inventory/working capital: INR60 crore inventory and INR20 crore die stock; watch whether inventory days fall toward one month.
Management declined to name customers under NDA and did not disclose the sub-sector split of the energy order book, limiting visibility.
key_quotes: Order book wise, if you see, for INR1,180 crores which we have mentioned, ratio wise, it is around 52% is from auto and 48% is from non -auto.
So, we do not have any hesitation in telling that we will achieve that figure going forward in next three years.
Dies will always be there, sir, for the entire top line, 7% to 8% of our sale is coming from die sale.
My all-fixed cost of plant 3 is already absorbed in my number.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, capacity and the INR1,000 crore FY30 ambition, but evasive on specifics such as margin split by sub-segment, customer names, aerospace funding and energy order book breakdown. Several answers were long and repetitive, and management often said it would confirm details later.

adds.what: Unit 3 expansion: melting capacity to 28,800 MT and casting/finishing to 12,600 MT by FY28 (from about 13,800 MT and 6,000 MT)
110 tons/month new casting and machining capacity (20% of 610 t/month total); machines booked post-IPO, delivery expected by September 2027

growth.why: Management reiterated about 50% FY27 revenue growth over INR294 crore FY26 base, backed by a INR1,180 crore order book (about INR630-640 crore execution next year) and Unit 3 capacity nearly doubling by FY28; however, the new capacity is largely not live until FY28 and the brief gives no detailed capex figure.
